title: perf(research): compile the P112 ten-deletion census with popcnt (2.69x, byte-identical receipts)
body:
## Summary
One-line verifier change: compile `research/p112-ten-deletion-span/census.cpp` with `-mpopcnt`.

The shipped `-O3` build compiles for baseline x86-64 without a `POPCNT` target feature, so every `count(Mask)` lowers to an opaque out-of-line call to libc `__popcountdi2`. Callgrind on a 5-rep budget-8 run attributes **25.04% of all retired instructions** to that call, and hiding it inside a function boundary also blocks loop vectorization around the census / `deletable` hot loops. The sibling packages `research/p112-common-deletion-slice` and `research/p112-common-fourteen-cut` (same PR3161 descent) already compile with `-mpopcnt`; this successor dropped it.

## Measured result
Same host (32-core Linux, gcc 15), same fixture, same interpreter, back-to-back builds differing only in the flag:

| invocation | before | after | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `census FIXTURE 8` | 39.10 s | 15.00 s | 2.61x |
| `census FIXTURE 10` | 99.69 s | 43.67 s | 2.28x |
| **full registered replay** (`verify.py --work`) | **155.94 s** | **57.91 s** | **2.69x** |

- Both census stdout streams are **byte-identical** before/after (`cmp` of the retained diagnostics), and the registered replay passes unchanged (`PASS_P112_TEN_DELETION_SPAN span=4 beta_5_4_remaining=2`, receipt compared to `RESULT.json` inside `verify.py`, no `--output`).
- `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` PASS; registered command 2 (`test_verify.py`, `-O -Werror`) PASS.
- `mpopcnt` is available on the committed replay hardware (the dedicated workflow runs only `ubuntu-latest` GH runners); outputs are unaffected because popcount semantics are target-independent.

## Scope
- `research/p112-ten-deletion-span/verify.py` only (+1 line in `FLAGS`). No census source change, no mathematical claim, no receipt, no other package.

Cross-references the measured handoff in #1166.
